classification.difficultyReason: Construct a multistage proof using vertically opposite angles, supplementary angles, alternate angles and the triangle angle sum.

content.prompt: Show that triangle $ABC$ is equilateral. Give full reasoning for each stage of your working.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with extended parallel lines GBAI and FCD, transversal HAC, and transversal BCE. Preserve all nine point labels, matching parallel arrows and the two given angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: G, B, A, I are collinear in that order; F, C, D are collinear in that order; AB is parallel to CD; H, A, C are collinear; B, C, E are collinear; angle HAI is 60 degrees and angle ECF is 120 degrees. Coordinates preserve these relationships without introducing printed measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens 60 degrees and 120 degrees are visible. No derived angles or proof are printed in the question diagram.

answer.short: $\angle BAC=\angle ABC=\angle ACB=60^{\circ}$, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.

inlines.text: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
The angles in a triangle sum to 180°.
